testEnvironment:
Test environment: the snapshot is a git repository whose single commit holds
the reviewed tree — its tree hash was compared against the commit under review
when the snapshot was cut. A suite run here collects and runs what a checkout at
that commit does, so a failing or skipped test is a fact about the tree, not
about this copy of it. Its history is that one synthetic commit: 'git log',
'git diff' and every ancestry question answer about the snapshot and never about
the PR.
The Recipe's Test entrypoint and Check step do not run these merge-gating CI steps, and nothing in this review ran them: rebase-check job (pull_request-only branch-currency assertion, not meaningful in a worktree of origin/main); proc-macos job (node --test tests/proc.test.mjs on macOS) (subsumed by the full suite on this macOS host); smoke-omp job (needs pinned omp installed via bun, absent here); install-and-smoke job (needs pinned omp installed via bun and network, absent here).

survived.claim: gateVerdictRefusal() compares only the Gate-verdict words of a row's old and new text, so a `ledger.mjs row` rewrite that keeps every verdict word but changes the row's PR mapping (impl-10=PR#40 → PR#41) moves the verdicts off PR 40, and finisher-pr-40 then dispatches past its dispositions-mismatch. This defeats mechanism 4's 'row refuses to drop a Gate verdict'.
survived.evidence: Ran `node --test --test-name-pattern='mismatch row away' tests/zz-probe-race.test.mjs` in my copy (ledger-dispositions fixture). The verb wrote `dispositions-mismatch=fix-pr-40:run-Rv40Aa01` (exit 1). The control `dispatch 40 finisher-pr-40` exited 2: 'dispositions mismatch — … not dispatching finisher-pr-40'. Then `row 10 "impl-10=PR#41 → PR#41 · review=member:review-pr-40 · reviewed=…:2/1/1:run-Rv40Aa01 · fix-pr-40=applied:… · dispositions-mismatch=fix-pr-40:run-Rv40Aa01"` exited 0 with only 'dropped: impl-10=PR#40 PR#40'. After that, `dispatch 40 finisher-pr-40` exited 0 with 'dispatched finisher-pr-40', and the rows became ['#10 impl-10=PR#41 → PR#41 · … · dispositions-mismatch=fix-pr-40:…', '#40 finisher-pr-40']. A second probe (correctness/p1/relocate.mjs) shows the same move for a reviewed= token on a plain `#50 PR#40 note` row: deriveRun then reports reviewed for pr 41, not 40.
survived.suggested_fix: In gateVerdictRefusal (or in the row command next to it), when the old row holds any Gate verdict, refuse a rewrite where rowNums(oldRow).pr !== rowNums(line).pr: moving a verdict to another PR's stream drops it from its own. Add a ledger-row-review test that changes the impl-<N>=PR#<M> outcome, or the first PR# mention, on a row carrying a verdict.

survived.claim: runDispositions checks the escalate-answer preconditions (the current verdict is an escalate from this member, and no fix-applier is live) only against the ledger it read before taking the lock. After acquireLock() and load() it appends the answer tokens and replaces the member's verdict without checking again, so two answer runs that both read the same escalate both write. The row then holds contradictory answers and an ok verdict, and the finisher dispatches.
survived.evidence: In my copy I ran a probe test built on the ledger-dispositions fixture: `escalated(f.check())`, then run B `dispositions fix-pr-40 --uphold 'survived[0]'`, with the stub's existing FAKE_GH_HOOK running run A `--send-back 'survived[0]'` once while B read the tracker. A exited 1 and recorded 'survived[0] sent back'. B exited 0 with verdict ok. Final row: '… · escalation-answer=run-Rv40Aa01:survived[0]:sent-back · escalation-answer=run-Rv40Aa01:survived[0]:upheld · dispositions-ok=fix-pr-40:run-Rv40Aa01'. Then `dispatch 40 finisher-pr-40` exited 0 ('dispatched finisher-pr-40'), and re-running the verb with no answers gave exit 1, verdict mismatch: escalationAnswers() reads the pair as sent-back, but the gate already let the finisher through. Before this PR, the check's whole-row `row` rewrite would have replaced A's tokens with B's (warning 'dropped:'), leaving a consistent upheld+ok row.
survived.suggested_fix: After `await acquireLock(); data = load();` and before writing answers (result.recorded.length > 0), run the recording preconditions again on the reloaded data: deriveRun(...).reviewed for the PR must still have run === result.run, dispositions an escalate from result.member, and fixLive empty. If not, die exit 2 with nothing written and say to run the verb again. Better still, judge again under the lock when the reloaded rows of that PR differ from the snapshot. The ADR's claim that a stale verdict 'does nothing' covers only a superseded review, not a second writer on the same review.

unverified.claim: isDispositionsWord matches the dispositions prefixes in any case but matches `escalation-answer=` case-sensitively, so `ledger.mjs token` accepts `Escalation-Answer=…` as a freeform token. This is harmless today because ESCALATION_ANSWER and every reader are case-sensitive too. It is an asymmetry to keep in mind if a reader ever parses that prefix case-insensitively.
unverified.evidence: Read only, not executed: ledger-grammar.mjs:455 `/^dispositions-(?:ok|mismatch|escalate|unchecked)=/i.test(word) || word.startsWith("escalation-answer=")`, and :300 ESCALATION_ANSWER has no /i flag.
unverified.suggested_fix: No change needed now. If one is wanted, add a comment saying the case-sensitive match is deliberate because the answer regex is case-sensitive.

unverified.claim: `ledger.mjs dispositions` judges against the pre-lock ledger and, after taking the lock, does not re-check that the review is still the latest. A review superseded in between still gets its verdict written, exits 0 and prints `ok`, and nothing on stderr or stdout says it was superseded.
unverified.evidence: Probe: the gh stub ran `ledger.mjs review 40 review=… reviewed=<head>:1/0/0:run-NewRun01` during the first `gh issue view`. The verb then exited 0 with stdout `{"verdict":"ok","token":"dispositions-ok=fix-pr-40:run-Rv40Aa01",...}`. stderr held only `wrote …/ledger.md`. The row ended `… reviewed=…:run-Rv40Aa01 · … · reviewed=…:run-NewRun01 · dispositions-ok=fix-pr-40:run-Rv40Aa01`. The new review's gate reads only verdicts naming run-NewRun01, so the finisher stays blocked as 'dispositions unchecked'. fleet-event.mjs reports `dispositions checked (exit 0)`. The header comment documents this ('does nothing'), so it is by design, but the no-op is silent and reports success.
unverified.suggested_fix: After `data = load()`, recompute the latest reviewed run for the PR. If it differs from `result.run`, print a stderr note (or refuse with exit 2) saying the verdict was written for a superseded review, so fleet-event can NEED a re-run rather than note 'checked (exit 0)'.

unverified.claim: The new contract text says 'its exit 1 is a verdict, any other nonzero exit a NEED'. An uncaught exception in the verb exits 1 under node, so a crash inside the in-process judgement would be noted as `dispositions checked (exit 1)`, with empty stdout and no token written. `ledger.mjs dispositions` installs no uncaught-exception handler that maps a crash to exit 2.
unverified.evidence: `grep -n 'uncaught\|unhandledRejection\|process.on(' plugin/scripts/ledger.mjs` shows only the `exit` and signal handlers (SIGTERM/SIGINT/SIGHUP → exit(2)). fleet-event.mjs treats `r.status === 0 || r.status === 1` as checked. I found no input that triggers an uncaught throw: the 330-case fuzz and the environment-fault probes all ended in exit 0/1/2 with a message. The old standalone script had the same exit-1-on-crash behaviour, and in-process judgement widens the code that can reach it. Unexercised hazard, so only a suggestion.
unverified.suggested_fix: In runDispositions, wrap `refusing`/the post-lock write so a non-CheckRefusal throw calls die() with exit 2. Alternatively, have fleet-event treat exit 1 with empty stdout as a NEED.

unverified.claim: A nonexistent `--repo` surfaces as `could not resolve --git-common-dir: spawnSync git ENOENT`, which reads as 'git is not installed' when the cause is a missing cwd. The diff's new in-process path (`readLabelMap({cwd: repo})` → refuse(e.message)) passes the misleading text straight through. The message itself comes from fleet-dir, outside the diff.
unverified.evidence: Probe `ledger.mjs … dispositions fix-pr-40 --scratch S --repo /nonexistent/x` exited 2 with stderr `ledger: could not resolve --git-common-dir: spawnSync git ENOENT`. Standalone with `--repo /nonexistent/x` printed the same cause. It exits 2 (a refusal, not swallowed), but names the wrong cause.
unverified.suggested_fix: Check that `repo` exists and is a directory in judgeMember or main before the first git or fleet-dir call, and refuse with 'no such repository path'.

unverified.claim: The `reviewed=` half of malformedGateWord is not discriminated by any test: deleting it leaves the whole narrowed suite green. gateVerdictRefusal(row, row+' · reviewed=zzz') should refuse as an unparseable Gate-verdict-shaped word, and no test asserts that.
unverified.evidence: Mutation: `(isDispositionsWord(word) || word.startsWith("reviewed=")) && !isGateVerdict` → `(isDispositionsWord(word)) && !isGateVerdict`. Result: ./agent-test tests/ledger-grammar.test.mjs → exit 0, tests 63, pass 63, fail 0 (mutant survives). Baseline on the unmutated tree: same command → exit 0, 63 pass. The unmutated function does return "adds 'reviewed=zzz', a word shaped like a Gate verdict…". In `row`, addedReviewToken refuses the same word first, so the branch is reachable only by calling gateVerdictRefusal directly. The `row` and `token` tests do not reach it either, so only a direct gateVerdictRefusal assertion would pin it.
unverified.suggested_fix: Add `assert.match(gateVerdictRefusal(row, `${row} · reviewed=zzz`), /adds 'reviewed=zzz'/)` to the gateVerdictRefusal test, or drop the redundant branch.

unverified.claim: judgeMember's contract is documented but not enforced by its signature. `ledger` and `reviewPath` are two independent optional parameters, and exactly one is meant to be set: reviewPath names the review when there is no ledger, and with a ledger the review comes off the ledger. The check for this lives only in the CLI main() (`arg("review") === null` → die). The `--review and a ledger contradict` guard was removed.
unverified.evidence: Read lines 925-1000 and 1105-1130. With a ledger, line 989 overwrites reviewPath with the path derived from the ledger, so a caller's reviewPath is silently ignored. With ledger=null and reviewPath=null, readJson(null) throws a TypeError. line 995 catches it and refuses with 'could not read the review file null: …', so it fails safe but with a misleading message. I ran judgeMember({name:'fix-pr-5',scratch:'/nonexistent',repo:'/tmp'}) from a non-git directory. It threw CheckRefusal at the git-common-dir step, before reaching that path. I did not reproduce the null-path message in a git repo.
unverified.suggested_fix: Take a discriminated input, e.g. `{ledger}` or `{reviewPath}` as one `source` argument. At minimum, refuse at the top of judgeMember when ledger === null && reviewPath === null, and when both are set.

unverified.claim: The verdict result's `run` and `token` are nullable together, exactly when ledger === null. That coupling is implicit, and ledger.mjs runDispositions destructures `{pr, run, token}` and writes `token` without a null check. It depends on having passed a non-null ledger.
unverified.evidence: Line 1074: `const token = ledger === null ? null : ...`. ledger.mjs runDispositions always passes `ledger: data`, so the path is safe today. Nothing in the result type ties token's non-nullness to that.
unverified.suggested_fix: Have runDispositions assert result.token !== null, or split the ledger-bound judgement from the standalone one so the two return shapes are distinct.

unverified.claim: CheckRefusal is a bare `class CheckRefusal extends Error {}` with no `name`. The two callers that distinguish it, main() and ledger.mjs's `refusing`, rely on `instanceof`. That works only while the module is loaded once, which is true for a dynamic import of the same file URL.
unverified.evidence: Lines 734 and 1119 (`if (e instanceof CheckRefusal) die(e.message)`), and the `await import("./dispositions-check.mjs")` in ledger.mjs runDispositions. A single module instance, so `instanceof` holds. Not exercised across duplicate module instances.
unverified.suggested_fix: Optional: set this.name = 'CheckRefusal'. This is low risk.

unverified.claim: judgeMember's `if (recording && ledger === null) refuse("--uphold and --send-back record … no ledger is in use")` cannot be reached from either caller. The standalone CLI never passes `listed`, so `recording` is false. The verb passes `ledger: data`, which is load()'s non-null object for every cmd except `rotate`. Nothing tests it either.
unverified.evidence:
1. grep `judgeMember(` in plugin and tests found exactly 2 calls: dispositions-check.mjs:1129 `judgeMember({ name, scratch, repo, reviewPath: arg("review") })`, with no `listed`, so it defaults to `new Map()`; and ledger.mjs:3208 `judgeMember({ … ledger: data, listed })`. ledger.mjs:722 is `let data = cmd === "rotate" ? null : load();`, and load() (ledger.mjs:504-) returns an object on every path.
2. grep 'no ledger is in use' in tests: 0 hits.
3. Mutation in the scratch copy: deleted lines 929-931, then ran `./agent-test tests/dispositions-check.test.mjs tests/ledger-dispositions.test.mjs tests/ledger-grammar.test.mjs tests/fleet-event.test.mjs tests/ledger-row-review.test.mjs tests/ledger-dispatch.test.mjs`. Result: exit=0, tests 556, pass 556, fail 0.
unverified.suggested_fix: Delete the three-line guard. Every remaining `recording` use (the `if (recording)` at ~968, inside `if (ledger !== null)`, and the one at ~1041) is unchanged. To keep the precondition documented, state it in judgeMember's JSDoc (`listed` non-empty only with a `ledger`) rather than as a runtime branch no caller can take.
